site.name: climate-almanac
site.summary: Climate Almanac — multi-variable climate explorer (local demo) Fictional climate-data explorer. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Explorer Three-panel layout: left rail variable selector (six climate variables, each with a colored swatch, units, and source caption), center chart area, right inspector panel. Center stack: - A vector chart with up to four overlaid series and a dual-axis option (left axis for unit-less anomalies, right for absolute units). - Hovering exposes a value tooltip and updates the right-rail inspector with the same year's values.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full climate-almanac system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Climate Almanac provides a robust multi-variable charting experience on desktop, but suffers from significant UX and accessibility flaws, particularly on mobile. Critical issues include an unenforced 4-variable limit that contradicts UI copy, broken interactive controls (dropdowns, annotation button, and dead navigation links), and severe mobile usability barriers due to tiny tap targets and unresponsive select elements. Untested areas include the 'NSIDC Sea Ice Index' source link and the 'Surface temperature anomaly' checkbox on desktop.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Climate Almanac data visualization tool, validating all interactive controls, chart states, and responsive layouts.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed through four phases, starting with the primary data visualization flow by manipulating variables, regions, and smoothing options. Next, it will validate chart interactions like hovering, zooming, and annotations, followed by testing utility actions like sharing and downloading. Finally, the entire flow will be re-validated on a mobile viewport to assess responsive behavior and layout warnings.
assumptions: The application is a single-page app contained entirely within index.html, with no actual routing for the Datasets, Stories, Methods, and About links.
The 'Share view' button will likely copy a URL to the clipboard or open a modal, and 'Download .csv' will trigger a file download.
The chart supports a maximum of four overlaid series based on the 'Add up to four variables' hint.
Small tap target warnings for checkboxes and nav links will be particularly problematic on mobile viewports.
risk_hotspots: Checkbox inputs for variables (13x13px tap targets) failing mobile accessibility guidelines
Layer reordering drag-and-drop functionality potentially failing on touch/mobile devices
State management when toggling between 'Dual axes' and 'Single (z-scored)' with multiple variables selected
Handling of the 4-variable limit (e.g., whether appropriate feedback is given if a 5th is selected)

phases.title: Variable Selection and Configuration
phases.objective: Validate the left rail controls for selecting climate variables, regions, smoothing, and axis modes.
key_checks: Toggle each of the 6 variable checkboxes and verify chart updates accordingly
Attempt to select more than 4 variables to test the limit enforcement and user feedback
Change the Region dropdown to 'Arctic (60°N–90°N)' and verify data updates
Cycle through Smoothing options (3-year, 10-year, 30-year) and observe chart transformations
Switch Y-AXIS radio from 'Dual axes' to 'Single (z-scored)' and verify axis scaling changes
exit_criteria: Region and Smoothing dropdowns have been changed and reverted
Y-axis mode has been switched successfully

phases.title: Chart Interaction and Inspector
phases.objective: Validate the central chart area interactions, the right inspector panel, and annotation features.
key_checks: Hover over the chart and verify the tooltip appears and the right-rail Inspector updates with year values
Click the '+ Note' button and verify an annotation can be added to the chart
Dismiss an existing annotation using the '×' button and verify it disappears
Click 'Reset zoom' if zoom is applicable, or verify its presence/state
Attempt to drag layers to reorder them in the 'LAYERS DRAG TO REORDER' section
exit_criteria: Inspector panel has been populated via hover
Layer order changed via drag interaction

phases.title: Utility Actions and Navigation
phases.objective: Test the top-bar utility actions and secondary navigation links.
key_checks: Click 'Share view' and verify the outcome (clipboard copy, modal, or URL update)
Click 'Download .csv' and verify a file is downloaded or appropriate action occurs
Click the 'Datasets', 'Stories', 'Methods', and 'About' links to check for dead ends or modals
exit_criteria: Share and Download actions have been triggered
All top navigation links have been clicked and behavior observed

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-test critical flows and assess layout adaptability on a mobile viewport, focusing on identified small tap targets.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify the three-panel layout adapts (e.g., stacks vertically)
Attempt to select variables using the small 13x13px checkboxes on mobile
Interact with the chart (hover/tap) to verify Inspector panel updates on mobile
Verify dropdowns (Region, Smoothing) are usable on a touch screen
Check if drag-to-reorder layers works via touch interactions
exit_criteria: Mobile layout has been visually verified
Primary configuration and interaction flows completed on mobile
Tap target usability has been assessed

coverage_targets.features: 100% of left-rail controls, chart interactions, and top-bar actions exercised
coverage_targets.mobile: Full repeat of variable selection, chart interaction, and layout validation on mobile viewport

notes: Pay close attention to how the chart handles the transition between 'Dual axes' and 'Single (z-scored)' when variables with different units (e.g., °C and ppm) are selected.
Since it's a local demo, 'Download .csv' might be blocked by browser restrictions; log any errors.
Drag-and-drop for layer reordering might be implemented via a JS library; verify it doesn't break on mobile touch events.

findings.user_goal: Overlay up to four climate variables on the chart
findings.problem: The UI explicitly states 'Add up to four variables to overlay', but the limit is completely unenforced. Users can select 5 or 6 variables without any warning or error, contradicting the stated constraint and potentially cluttering the chart.
findings.evidence: Session memory notes: 'Attempting to select a 5th variable (Arctic sea-ice extent) when 4 are already active successfully added it to the LAYERS list, violating the stated Add up to four variables constraint' and 'the UI successfully allowed toggling a 6th variable (ENSO ONI)'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on instructional copy to understand system limits. Violating this stated limit breaks trust and creates confusion about whether the application is functioning correctly.
findings.suggestion: Enforce the 4-variable limit by disabling unselected checkboxes when 4 are active, and display a clear tooltip or inline message explaining why further selections are disabled.

findings.user_goal: Select Region and Smoothing options on a mobile device
findings.problem: The Region and Smoothing dropdowns are broken on the mobile viewport. Selecting an option either reverts to a default or selects the wrong item entirely, making these core configuration controls unusable on touch devices.
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunk steps-37-42 shows: 'Selecting Arctic (60°N–90°N) from the Region dropdown failed; the tool feedback indicates it selected Global instead' and 'Region dropdown failed to update to Southern Hemisphere; tool feedback indicates it selected Northern Hemisphere instead'.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users are completely blocked from filtering data by region or smoothing, rendering the explorer's primary analytical features inaccessible to them.
findings.suggestion: Debug the select element event handling on mobile/touch events to ensure the selected value correctly updates the application state and chart data.

findings.user_goal: Toggle variables, axes, and remove layers on a mobile device
findings.problem: Interactive controls for checkboxes, radio buttons, and layer removal ('×') have critically small tap targets (13x13px and 20x17px), far below the 44px minimum mobile guidance.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag these elements: 'Variable checkboxes in the left rail have critically small tap targets (13x13px)' and 'Layer removal button (×) is only 20x17px'.
findings.why_it_matters: Touch users will struggle to accurately tap these tiny targets, leading to frustration, mis-taps, and an overall inaccessible mobile experience.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding around native inputs to expand the tap area to at least 44x44px, or replace them with custom styled controls that meet mobile touch guidelines.
findings.source_hint: index.html: ux-3 to ux-8 (checkboxes), ux-11/ux-12 (radios), ux-55 (× button)

findings.user_goal: Add an annotation to the chart
findings.problem: Clicking the '+ Note' button produces no visible change, modal, or inline input form on either desktop or mobile, failing to provide any user feedback or path to complete the action.
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunk steps-07-12 and steps-43-48 confirm: 'Clicking the + Note button produced no visible change, no modal, and no inline input form' on both desktop and mobile viewports.
findings.why_it_matters: A button that appears interactive but does nothing creates a false affordance, confusing users and making the app appear broken.
findings.suggestion: Either implement the annotation flow (e.g., open a modal or inline text field) or disable/hide the button if the feature is not yet available, providing a tooltip explaining its future state.

findings.user_goal: Access Stories, Methods, and source information
findings.problem: Navigation links ('Stories', 'Methods') and source links ('Berkeley Earth', 'NOAA', 'CMIP6', 'NSIDC') are dead-ends (href='#') that provide no content, modal, or visual feedback when clicked.
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunks steps-19-24 note: 'Clicking the Stories navigation link resulted in no visible change... confirming it is a dead-end' and 'Source links in the left rail appear to be non-functional placeholders'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect links to provide additional context or navigate to resources. Dead links break the user journey and erode trust in the data provenance.
findings.suggestion: Remove placeholder links or provide a visual indicator (e.g., 'Coming soon' tooltip) if the content is not yet available. For source links, ensure they point to the actual external references.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Nav links (Stories, Methods), SOURCES section links

findings.user_goal: Use the Region and Smoothing dropdowns accessibly
findings.problem: The Region and Smoothing select elements lack associated label elements, aria-labels, or placeholders, failing accessibility standards.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag: 'A form field has no label, aria-label, or placeholder' for both ux-9 and ux-10.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not know the purpose of these dropdowns, making the core data filtering features completely inaccessible to them.
findings.suggestion: Add visible <label> elements associated with the select elements, or at minimum, add aria-label attributes to describe their purpose.

findings.problem: The 'Reset zoom' button lacks a disabled state or feedback when the chart is already at its default zoom level, leaving users uncertain if their click registered.
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunk steps-13-18 states: 'Clicking Reset zoom when the chart is already at its default range produces no visible change or textual feedback'.
findings.why_it_matters: Without a disabled state or notification, users may click repeatedly, thinking the button is broken rather than realizing zoom is already reset.
findings.suggestion: Visually disable the 'Reset zoom' button when no zoom is applied, or display a brief toast message indicating the view is already at the default range.

findings.user_goal: Apply 10-year running mean smoothing to the chart
findings.problem: Selecting '10-year running mean' from the Smoothing dropdown fails to update the chart subtitle and reverts to 'No smoothing', indicating a state management or reactivity bug.
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunk steps-07-12 notes: 'Selecting 10-year running mean from the Smoothing dropdown failed to update the chart subtitle, which still displays 3-year running mean' and 'the selection reverted to No smoothing'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot reliably apply the 10-year smoothing option, limiting their ability to analyze long-term climate trends as intended.
findings.suggestion: Debug the event handler and state update logic for the Smoothing dropdown to ensure all options correctly update the chart data and subtitle.

gaps: 44% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
